messages:
olivia: Hi all 111 I'm on my first day and hitting a snag with kubectl on WSL2. I pasted the kubeconfig from the onboarding site but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows contexts, then `kubectl get ns` returns `Unauthorized`. Any quick onboarding tips?

ben: Welcome! Two common WSL traps: 1) Windows CRLF in the kubeconfig (breaks base64 certs), 2) missing exec credential helper for our Okta flow. Run `file ~/.kube/config` and `dos2unix ~/.kube/config` if it says CRLF.

olivia: `file` shows "with CRLF line terminators". Ran `dos2unix` and now `kubectl get ns` moved to `exec plugin: invalid token: token expired`.

tara: For Okta we use `kubelogin`. Do `kubelogin --login` from WSL; it opens a browser on Windows to complete SSO. Make sure the `kubelogin` binary is the Linux one inside WSL (we keep it at `~/.local/bin`).

olivia: Ran `kubelogin --login` and completed the browser flow. Namespaces show now, progress! Thanks. Quick follow-up: tried `kubectl get pods -n infra` and got `Forbidden`. What's the standard request flow for namespace access?

ben: We prefer a GitHub PR in infra/access-requests with the RoleBinding YAML, or use the Access Portal (link in the onboarding doc). In the PR, include your redwood username, namespaces, desired role (view/edit), and a short justification. Ping @ben or @tara for a fast review.

olivia: Filed PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4201 - requested `view` on `infra` and `staging` for debugging deploy issues.

infra-bot: Access request PR #4201 opened by olivia. Automated tests passed.

tara: Approved and applied. You should have `view` in both namespaces now.

ben: confirm with `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra`

olivia: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n infra` -> "yes". All good. Thanks y'all :tada:`
